title: レトロゲームエンジン
subtitle: Lyre3 GamesのPyxelをめぐる3つの実装
author: ミューズさん
summary: Lyre3 Gamesでは、レトロゲームエンジンを作り、そのエンジンでゲームを作っています。その題材であるPyxelをめぐる3つの実装を比べます。Pythonで書く本家、そのAPIをRustとWASMの軽い経路へ移したpyxel-rust、互換を追わずGPUで3Dを描くrustgames。GitHubでは「フォーク」と登録されながら中身は独立に作った、pyxel-rustの生い立ちも紹介します。

en.title: Retro Game Engines
en.subtitle: Three Pyxel Implementations by Lyre3 Games
en.summary: At Lyre3 Games, we build retro game engines and create games using them. We compare three implementations of Pyxel, our subject of study: the original written in Python; pyxel-rust, which ported its API to a lightweight Rust and WASM path; and rustgames, which renders 3D on the GPU without pursuing compatibility. We also introduce the origins of pyxel-rust—a project created independently despite being listed as a "fork" on GitHub.
en.cover_alt: An illustration showing three branches extending from a single root, each tipped with a retro game screen (a maze and snake, a spaceship and gears, and a neon 3D tunnel).
en.html:
At Lyre3 Games, we build retro game engines and create games using them. Our focus is a small retro game engine called Pyxel. Around me, there are three different implementations of Pyxel, each built differently: the original, and my own, which carries on its name.

First, let's talk about the lineage.

On GitHub, my pyxel-rust is listed as a "fork" of the original kitao/pyxel. This is because the record of the fork from March 2026 remains intact. However, the original version at the time of the fork (Pyxel v2.7.10) is simply left untouched on the main branch.

The master branch I've actually been developing has an independent history, sharing no common ancestor with the original. This includes 431 commits from May to June 2026, which I worked on alongside Copilot. In other words, despite being called a "fork," it has a somewhat unusual origin—it's essentially something entirely different, built from scratch.

The Original Pyxel — Easy with Python

The original Pyxel is an engine for writing games in Python. Its main selling point is its ease of use, allowing you to test ideas as soon as they come to mind. The engine's core is built in Rust, and when running it on the web, it uses a method (called Emscripten) that delivers the entire Python runtime to the browser. The strength of the original version lies in its well-organized "engine as a distribution."

pyxel-rust — Bringing the API world to Rust and WASM

pyxel-rust is an implementation that ports the original API ecosystem to a lightweight Rust and WASM pipeline. The game itself is written in Rust and converted directly to WASM using wasm-bindgen. Browser rendering primarily relies on Canvas 2D, though a WGPU-based rendering method is also available. Core APIs from the original—such as init, run, cls, blt, and text—are not simply ported code, but compatible implementations rebuilt to ensure identical usage. On desktop, there is also an option to use the original pyxel-core (SDL2) for the rendering side. Python-based tools (run, app2html) are also included, and GitHub Pages hosts a series of demos (such as Arisa Quest) that can be played in the browser.

rustgames ― 3D without chasing compatibility

rustgames is a completely original implementation with no lineage to Pyxel. It is an engine and a collection of games built with Rust, wgpu, and WebGL, designed for 3D rendering on the GPU from the ground up. The engine features built-in mechanisms such as fog, point light sources, automatic maze generation, enemy AI pathfinding, FPS-style cameras, and particles. It includes 3D games like Neon Maze 3D, Neon Blast 3D, and Earth Defense, which can be played in the browser via the play page. A JavaScript engine library (engine.js) is also available.

Side by side

Original Pyxel pyxel-rust rustgames
Language for writing games Python Rust Rust
Browser execution Bundled with Python runtime Directly converted to WASM Directly converted to WASM
Rendering Built-in engine Canvas 2D/wgpu wgpu/WebGL (3D)
Compatibility with original API Original itself Compatible implementations of key APIs Not aimed for
Positioning Engine included in distribution 2D implementation that moved the API landscape to a lighter path Full-fledged GPU-based 3D rendering

In a nutshell

The original is "an engine for easily creating and distributing projects in Python." pyxel-rust is "a 2D implementation that moves that API landscape to a lightweight Rust/WASM path." rustgames is "a lineage that doesn't chase compatibility, rendering 3D on the GPU from the start."

Even when "making a game," the character of the final product changes depending on the language and execution path. I believe the choice of foundation directly shapes the character of the work.

Continued in Measurement Section

"So, which one is actually faster?" We won't know until we measure it. Right now, I'm preparing to run two games—CubeBoy and LINE BOY—using three approaches—the original Pyxel, pyxel-rust, and vanilla JavaScript—to compare their startup speed, frame rate, and the amount of data loaded. Once the results are in, I'll report them in a follow-up.

At Lyre3 Games, we build retro game engines and create games using them. Our focus is a small retro game engine called Pyxel. Around me, there are three different implementations of Pyxel, each built differently: the original, and my own, which carries on its name.

## First, let's talk about the lineage.

On GitHub, my [pyxel-rust](https://github.com/oosawak/pyxel-rust) is listed as a "fork" of the original [kitao/pyxel](https://github.com/kitao/pyxel). This is because the record of the fork from March 2026 remains intact. However, the original version at the time of the fork (Pyxel v2.7.10) is simply left untouched on the main branch.

The master branch I've actually been developing has an independent history, sharing no common ancestor with the original. This includes 431 commits from May to June 2026, which I worked on alongside Copilot. In other words, despite being called a "fork," it has a somewhat unusual origin—it's essentially something entirely different, built from scratch.

## The Original Pyxel — Easy with Python

The original [Pyxel](https://github.com/kitao/pyxel) is an engine for writing games in Python. Its main selling point is its ease of use, allowing you to test ideas as soon as they come to mind. The engine's core is built in Rust, and when running it on the web, it uses a method (called Emscripten) that delivers the entire Python runtime to the browser. The strength of the original version lies in its well-organized "engine as a distribution."

## pyxel-rust — Bringing the API world to Rust and WASM

[pyxel-rust](https://github.com/oosawak/pyxel-rust) is an implementation that ports the original API ecosystem to a lightweight Rust and WASM pipeline. The game itself is written in Rust and converted directly to WASM using wasm-bindgen. Browser rendering primarily relies on Canvas 2D, though a WGPU-based rendering method is also available. Core APIs from the original—such as init, run, cls, blt, and text—are not simply ported code, but compatible implementations rebuilt to ensure identical usage. On desktop, there is also an option to use the original pyxel-core (SDL2) for the rendering side. Python-based tools (run, app2html) are also included, and GitHub Pages hosts a series of demos (such as Arisa Quest) that can be played in the browser.

## rustgames ― 3D without chasing compatibility

[rustgames](https://github.com/oosawak/rustgames) is a completely original implementation with no lineage to Pyxel. It is an engine and a collection of games built with Rust, wgpu, and WebGL, designed for 3D rendering on the GPU from the ground up. The engine features built-in mechanisms such as fog, point light sources, automatic maze generation, enemy AI pathfinding, FPS-style cameras, and particles. It includes 3D games like Neon Maze 3D, Neon Blast 3D, and Earth Defense, which can be played in the browser via the [play page](https://oosawak.github.io/rustgames/play/). A JavaScript engine library (engine.js) is also available.

## Side by side

|  | Original Pyxel | pyxel-rust | rustgames |
|---|---|---|---|
| Language for writing games | Python | Rust | Rust |
| Browser execution | Bundled with Python runtime | Directly converted to WASM | Directly converted to WASM |
| Rendering | Built-in engine | Canvas 2D/wgpu | wgpu/WebGL (3D) |
| Compatibility with original API | Original itself | Compatible implementations of key APIs | Not aimed for |
| Positioning | Engine included in distribution | 2D implementation that moved the API landscape to a lighter path | Full-fledged GPU-based 3D rendering |

## In a nutshell

The original is "an engine for easily creating and distributing projects in Python." pyxel-rust is "a 2D implementation that moves that API landscape to a lightweight Rust/WASM path." rustgames is "a lineage that doesn't chase compatibility, rendering 3D on the GPU from the start."

Even when "making a game," the character of the final product changes depending on the language and execution path. I believe the choice of foundation directly shapes the character of the work.

## Continued in Measurement Section

"So, which one is actually faster?" We won't know until we measure it. Right now, I'm preparing to run two games—CubeBoy and LINE BOY—using three approaches—the original Pyxel, pyxel-rust, and vanilla JavaScript—to compare their startup speed, frame rate, and the amount of data loaded. Once the results are in, I'll report them in a follow-up.

markdown:
Lyre3 Gamesでは、レトロゲームエンジンを作り、そのエンジンでゲームを作っています。\
題材にしているのは、Pyxel（ピクセル）という小さなレトロゲームエンジンです。\
私の周りには、このPyxelをめぐって、作り方の違う3つの実装があります。\
本家と、その名前を受け継いだ私の2つです。

## まず系譜の話から

GitHubの上では、私の[pyxel-rust](https://github.com/oosawak/pyxel-rust)は、本家[kitao/pyxel](https://github.com/kitao/pyxel)の「フォーク」として登録されています。\
2026年3月にフォークした記録が、そのまま残っているからです。\
ただし、フォークした時点の本家（Pyxel v2.7.10）は、mainブランチに手つかずで残してあるだけです。

実際に育ててきたmasterブランチは、本家と共通の祖先を持たない、独立した履歴になっています。\
2026年5月から6月にかけての431コミットがそれで、作業はCopilotと一緒に進めました。\
つまり「フォーク」と書いてあるのに、中身はゼロから作った別物、という少し変わった生い立ちです。

## 本家Pyxel ― Pythonで手軽に

本家の[Pyxel](https://github.com/kitao/pyxel)は、ゲームをPythonで書くエンジンです。\
書きやすさが売りで、思いついたらすぐ試せる手軽さがあります。\
エンジンの芯はRustで作られていて、Webで遊ばせるときはPythonの実行環境ごとブラウザへ運ぶ（Emscriptenという）方式です。\
「配布物としてのエンジン」がきちんと整っているのが、本家の強みです。

## pyxel-rust ― APIの世界をRustとWASMへ

[pyxel-rust](https://github.com/oosawak/pyxel-rust)は、本家のAPIの世界を、RustとWASMの軽い経路へ移した実装です。\
ゲーム自体をRustで書き、wasm-bindgenで直接WASMにします。\
ブラウザでの描画はCanvas 2Dが中心で、wgpuを使う描画方式も選べます。\
init／run／cls／blt／textといった本家の主要なAPIは、コードを持ってきたのではなく、同じ使い方になるよう作り直した互換実装です。\
デスクトップでは、本家のpyxel-core（SDL2）を描画側に使う選択肢もあります。\
Python製の道具（run／app2html）も付いていて、GitHub Pagesにはブラウザで遊べるデモ（Arisa Questなど）が並んでいます。

## rustgames ― 互換を追わない3D

[rustgames](https://github.com/oosawak/rustgames)は、Pyxelとは系譜の関係がない、完全な独自実装です。\
Rustとwgpu／WebGLで、最初からGPUで3Dを描くためのエンジンと、それで作ったゲーム集になっています。\
霧や点光源、迷路の自動生成、敵AIの経路探索、FPS視点のカメラ、パーティクルといった仕組みを、エンジン側に内蔵しています。\
Neon Maze 3D、Neon Blast 3D、Earth Defenseといった3Dゲームが入り、[プレイ用ページ](https://oosawak.github.io/rustgames/play/)からブラウザで遊べます。\
JavaScript側のエンジンライブラリ（engine.js）も持っています。

## 並べてみると

|  | 本家Pyxel | pyxel-rust | rustgames |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ゲームを書く言語 | Python | Rust | Rust |
| ブラウザでの動かし方 | Pythonの実行環境ごと運ぶ | WASMに直接変換 | WASMに直接変換 |
| 描画 | エンジン内蔵 | Canvas 2D／wgpu | wgpu／WebGL（3D） |
| 本家APIとの互換 | 本家そのもの | 主要APIを互換実装 | 目指さない |
| 位置づけ | 配布物のエンジン | APIの世界を軽い経路へ移した2D実装 | GPUで3Dを描く本格派 |

## 一言で言うと

本家は「Pythonで手軽に作る、配布物のエンジン」です。\
pyxel-rustは「そのAPIの世界を、RustとWASMの軽い経路へ移した2D実装」です。\
rustgamesは「互換を追わず、最初からGPUで3Dを描く系統」です。

同じ「ゲームを作る」でも、言語と実行の経路が違えば、できあがりの性格も変わります。\
土台の選び方が、そのまま作品の性格になるのだと思います。

## 計測編へ続く

「では、実際に速いのはどれなのか」。\
それは、測ってみないと分かりません。\
いま、CubeBoyとLINE BOYという2つのゲームを、本家Pyxel／pyxel-rust／素のJavaScriptの3つの方式で動かして、起動の速さやフレームレート、読み込むデータの量を比べる準備を進めています。\
結果が出たら、続編で報告します。
